title: Mankanya people - Wikipedia
text: The Mankanya people (Portuguese: Mancanha; French: Mancagne; self-designed as Ba-hula) are an ethnic group native to West Africa, more precisely the Senegambian region and Guinea.

title: Mankanya language - Wikipedia
text: Mankanya is known as "Uhula" by the people themselves (the Mankanya people, or "Bahula"). The name 'Mankanya' is thought to have been conferred upon the people and their language by colonialists who mistook the name of their chief at the time of colonisation for the name of the people-group itself. The language contains many loanwords from Kriol.

text: Mankanya is an endangered indigenous language of Guinea-Bissau and Senegal. It belongs to the Niger-Congo language family. The language is used as a first language by some people in every generation of the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
